features.description: The page tree: the pages in order, their inherited attributes, and inserting, moving, and deleting pages.
The standard security handler: user and owner passwords, permissions, and RC4 and AES encryption.
Characters, white space, delimiters, and comments of the file syntax.
Booleans, numbers, strings, names, arrays, dictionaries, streams, null, and indirect objects and references.
The ASCIIHexDecode filter: stream data as hexadecimal digits.
The ASCII85Decode filter: stream data in base-85 text.
The LZWDecode filter: LZW-compressed stream data, with its predictors.
The RunLengthDecode filter: byte-oriented run-length encoding.
The CCITTFaxDecode filter: Group 3 and Group 4 fax encoding of monochrome images.
The JBIG2Decode filter: JBIG2 monochrome images with their global segments.
The DCTDecode filter: JPEG baseline and progressive images.
The JPXDecode filter: JPEG 2000 images, with their own color and transparency.
The Crypt filter: decrypting one stream with a named crypt filter.
The header line that gives the file's PDF version.
The classic cross-reference table and the trailer that follows it.
Appending changes after the original bytes, with a new cross-reference section.
Compressed objects stored inside object streams.
Cross-reference data as a stream, and hybrid-reference files.
The encryption dictionary and the per-object keys of strings and streams.
Public-key security: recipients, their certificates, and their permissions.
Named crypt filters and their methods: RC4, AES-128, and AES-256.
The catalog: the root of the document's objects and its document-level settings.
Page objects: boxes, resources, contents, rotation, and user units.
The name dictionary: the name trees of destinations, attachments, scripts, and other named objects.
Content streams, their operators, and resource dictionaries.
Text strings in PDFDocEncoding, UTF-16BE, and UTF-8, and byte and ASCII strings.
Date strings with their time zone.
Name trees: sorted string keys spread over leaf and intermediate nodes.
Number trees: sorted integer keys spread over leaf and intermediate nodes.
Type 0 functions: sampled values with interpolation.
Type 2 functions: exponential interpolation between two values.
Type 3 functions: subfunctions joined over subdomains.
Type 4 functions: a PostScript calculator program.
File specifications: file names, URLs, and their platform forms.
Files embedded in the document, with their parameters and checksums.
Related files arrays: files that belong together with an embedded file.
Collection items: the field values of a file in a portable collection.
The extensions dictionary: developer and ISO extensions that a document uses.
The graphics state and its parameter dictionaries.
Path construction, painting, and clipping.
DeviceGray, DeviceRGB, and DeviceCMYK.
CalGray: calibrated gray.
CalRGB: calibrated RGB.
Lab: CIE L*a*b*.
ICCBased: color described by an embedded ICC profile.
Indexed: a color table over a base color space.
Pattern: painting with a tiling or shading pattern.
Separation: one colorant with its alternate space and tint transform.
DeviceN: several colorants, with their attributes and mixing hints.
Overprint and its mode.
Tiling patterns: a cell of content repeated over an area.
Type 1 shadings: color as a function of position.
Type 2 shadings: color varying along an axis.
Type 3 shadings: color varying between two circles.
Type 4 shadings: free-form Gouraud-shaded triangle meshes.
Type 5 shadings: lattice-form Gouraud-shaded triangle meshes.
Type 6 shadings: Coons patch meshes.
Type 7 shadings: tensor-product patch meshes.
Shading patterns and the sh operator.
External objects and the Do operator.
Image XObjects: samples, decoding, interpolation, and alternates.
Stencil masks, explicit masks, and color-key masking.
Images written inline in a content stream.
Form XObjects: reusable content with its own resources and matrix.
Reference XObjects: content imported from a page of another document.
Optional content groups, memberships, configurations, and their usage.
Character and word spacing, scaling, leading, rise, and rendering modes.
Text objects, positioning, and showing text.
Type 1 fonts, the standard 14 fonts, and multiple master fonts.
TrueType fonts as simple fonts.
Type 3 fonts: glyphs drawn by content streams.
Encodings of simple fonts: base encodings and differences.
CIDFonts: CIDFontType0 and CIDFontType2, with their widths and CID-to-GID maps.
CMaps: predefined and embedded maps from codes to CIDs.
Type 0 composite fonts.
Font descriptors: metrics, flags, and style.
Embedded font programs: Type 1, TrueType, CFF, and OpenType.
Mapping glyphs to Unicode, with ToUnicode CMaps.
Converting colors to device colors, with rendering intents.
Conversions among device color spaces, black generation, and undercolor removal.
Transfer functions.
Halftone screens and spot functions.
Flatness, smoothness, and stroke adjustment.
Separable and non-separable blend modes.
Soft masks from luminosity, alpha, and images.
Transparency groups: isolated and knockout groups.
Color spaces of groups and overprint with transparency.

Explicit and named destinations.
The document outline: bookmarks with their titles, actions, and styles.

Navigators that present a portable collection.

Article threads and their beads.
Page transitions and display durations.

Appearance streams of annotations: normal, rollover, and down.

Link annotations: areas that go to a destination or perform an action.

Line annotations, with their endings, leaders, and captions.
Square and circle annotations.
Polygon and polyline annotations.
Highlight, underline, squiggly, and strikeout annotations.
Caret annotations: where text is to be inserted.
Rubber stamp annotations.
Ink annotations: freehand paths.
Popup annotations that show the text of another annotation.
File attachment annotations: files attached at a point of a page.
Sound annotations.
Movie annotations.
Screen annotations: regions where media plays.
Widget annotations: the appearance and characteristics of form fields.
Printer's mark annotations.
Trap network annotations.
Watermark annotations, with their fixed print placement.
Redaction annotations: content marked for removal.
Projection annotations.
3D and RichMedia annotations.

Thread actions: going to an article bead.
URI actions and the document's base URI.
Sound actions.
Movie actions.
Hide actions: showing and hiding annotations.
Named actions such as next and previous page.
Actions that change the state of optional content groups.
Rendition actions: controlling media playback.
Transition actions.
Go-To-3D-view actions.
ECMAScript actions and document-level scripts.
Rich media execute actions.
Variable text: default appearance, quadding, and rich text of fields.

Push buttons, check boxes, and radio buttons.
Text fields: single line, multiline, password, file select, and comb.
Choice fields: list boxes and combo boxes.
Signature fields, their locks, and seed values.
Submit-form, reset-form, and import-data actions.
Forms Data Format files.
Forms flattened into page content.
Signature dictionaries, byte ranges, and their PKCS#7 and CAdES encodings.
Certification and field locking: DocMDP, FieldMDP, and UR transforms.
The document security store and validation-related information.
Document timestamp signatures.
The permissions dictionary of usage rights and certification.
Legal content attestations.
Viewports and measure dictionaries: rectilinear and geospatial.
Requirements that a viewer must meet to process the document.
Renditions, media clips, play and screen parameters, and media players.
Sound objects.
Movie dictionaries.
Alternate presentations: slide shows.
3D streams, views, nodes, lighting, and render modes.
Rich media content, configurations, instances, and settings.
The document information dictionary.
XMP metadata streams of the document and its components.
The trailer's file identifier pair.
Page-piece dictionaries: private data of applications.
Marked-content sequences and their property lists.
The structure tree, its elements, parent tree, attributes, and class map.
Structure namespaces and their role maps.
Tagged PDF: the mark information and the standard structure types and attributes.
Natural language, alternate descriptions, replacement text, and abbreviations.
Web capture: content sets, source information, and commands.
Media, crop, bleed, trim, and art boxes, and box color information.
Separation dictionaries of pre-separated pages.
Output intents and their destination profiles.
Trap networks and their regions.
Open prepress interface dictionaries.
Document parts: page ranges with their metadata.
Associated files of the document, its pages, and its objects.
Linearized files for incremental display over a network.

PDF/UA-1 and PDF/UA-2: accessible documents, read, written, and kept.
PDF/X: graphic exchange documents, read and kept.
PDF/VT: variable and transactional printing documents, read and kept.
